UnitStatement: The PRD is derived from repository-local sources only.
When documents and implementation disagree, the PRD states the product requirement and records the implementation note under Known Gaps and Risks.
Chirality is a desktop harness for running governed AI agents against a user-selected local filesystem workspace.
The desktop app packages a release-managed instruction root containing AGENTS.md, agents, docs, and framework files.
All project execution state remains in a user-selected working root named projectRoot.
The product accelerates deliverable-heavy professional work while preserving human authority, provenance, auditability, and filesystem-native state.
Agents support scope decomposition, scaffolding, document drafting, dependency extraction, semantic analysis, reconciliation, estimating, scheduling, and change management.
Agent outputs remain drafts or decision support until accepted by an accountable human.
Project truth lives in git-tracked plain files.
A decision that is not in a versioned file does not exist for purposes of reliance.
The product shall provide a local desktop application that runs agent workflows against a selected working root without requiring an external database.
The product shall preserve strict separation between the bundled instruction root and the mutable working root.
Agent work shall be auditable through plain files, git diffs, lifecycle files, dependency registers, and immutable snapshots.
The product shall provide matrix-based navigation into WORKBENCH for interactive persona agents and PIPELINE for operative task categories.
The product shall support streaming chat turns with session persistence, runtime options, interrupts, multimodal attachments, and Anthropic provider integration.

The product shall enforce safety and governance boundaries including human gates, no automated issuance, no hidden project memory, fail-closed subagent delegation, and Anthropic-only outbound network policy.
The product shall provide deterministic tools and validation workflows for scaffolding, schema checks, dependency closure, harness runtime validation, and release packaging.
The product shall ship a macOS 15+ Apple Silicon unsigned DMG build path with instruction-root integrity verification.
The product must not replace professional judgment or produce binding approval records autonomously.
The product must not sign, seal, certify, approve, issue, transmit, or otherwise release professional work for reliance.
The product must not make safety-critical decisions without human review.
The product must not conduct financial transactions or binding commitments.
The product must not depend on an external project database.
The product must not persist project truth in hidden app state, chats, caches, or vendor systems.
The product must not allow outbound network access beyond the Anthropic API path required for provider execution.
The product must not treat local UI preferences, API keys, or chat drafts as authoritative project state.
The Professional Operator selects the working root, approves gates, reviews evidence, and decides what can be relied upon.
The Project Orchestrator converts a scope of work into packages, deliverables, lifecycle records, document kits, dependency registers, and coordination artifacts.
The Project Orchestrator uses ORCHESTRATOR, WORKING_ITEMS, RECONCILIATION, CHANGE, and PIPELINE lanes.
The Specialist Contributor executes bounded deliverable-local work through TASK, DEPENDENCIES, CHIRALITY_FRAMEWORK, CHIRALITY_LENS, ESTIMATING, or audit agents.
The Governance Maintainer is responsible for agent instruction conformance, invariant consistency, deterministic tooling, and release-managed instruction-root changes.
The Release Operator builds, validates, packages, and distributes local unsigned desktop builds.
Project state is represented as human-readable files under the working root.
Review, audit, rollback, and approvals bind to git-tracked content.
Agents propose while humans approve, issue, sign, seal, and decide.
Claims require provenance, and unknowns become TBD rather than guesses.
Runtime convenience state is allowed only when it is explicitly non-authoritative.
Release-managed agent OS files must not be modified by project execution.
Each agent has an explicit write scope.
Derived outputs live in tool roots, while source truth lives in deliverable folders.
Snapshot-producing runs create timestamped folders that are not overwritten.
_LATEST.md pointers may move.
Rigor scales with stakes, and structure is added when it reduces error, rework, or ambiguity.

The current scope includes matrix navigation across PORTAL, WORKBENCH, and PIPELINE.
The current scope includes session lifecycle APIs and turn execution via SSE.
The current scope includes an Anthropic SDK provider path with local UI key storage and environment fallback.
The current scope includes stub provider mode for deterministic local tests.
The current scope includes server-side attachment resolution for supported file types.
The current scope includes an Operator Toolkit for per-turn runtime options and local presets.
The current scope includes execution-root scaffolding from decomposition markdown.
The current scope includes deliverable status and dependency contract APIs.
The current scope includes lifecycle transition enforcement for _STATUS.md.
The current scope includes Dependency register read and write support for Dependencies.csv v3.1.
The current scope includes subagent governance evaluation and fail-closed delegation behavior.
The current scope includes a deterministic tool registry for scaffolding, validation, reporting, coordination, PDF-to-markdown, and evaluation.
The current scope includes harness validation scripts and a CI premerge workflow.
The current scope includes instruction-root integrity verification in packaged builds.
The current scope includes a macOS Apple Silicon unsigned DMG packaging workflow.
The current release target includes macOS 15+.
The current release target includes Apple Silicon arm64.
The current release target is an unsigned, unnotarized local-builder DMG.
Development and build require Node.js version 20 or later.
README references Windows packaging, but the current build config and runbook define macOS arm64 as the concrete release target.
Automated staleness propagation and dirty-state SHA comparison are out of scope for the current release.
A deliverable-level lock mechanism is out of scope for the current release.
Unified pipeline run record persistence across all task agents is out of scope for the current release.
Project-level dependency graph visualization output is out of scope for the current release.
Automated merge gates beyond documented and human CHANGE constraints are out of scope for the current release.
Windows release packaging is out of scope unless separately scoped.
A runtime enforcement monitor that intercepts every agent file write is out of scope for the current release.
Working-root selection starts when the user opens Chirality.
The user can enter an absolute path or choose a folder through the native Electron directory picker.
The app validates that the selected path exists, is a directory, is readable and writable, and is not inside the instruction root.
The app stores the selected root as local UI state and uses it for file tree, scan, chat session, scaffold, and contract APIs.
Relative working-root paths are rejected.
Missing or inaccessible working-root directories show actionable errors.
Instruction-root conflicts are blocked during working-root selection.
Clearing the working root disables runtime actions that require projectRoot.
Matrix navigation starts when the user enters PORTAL.
Selecting a NORMATIVE or EVALUATIVE matrix cell routes to WORKBENCH with agent context.
Selecting an OPERATIVE matrix cell routes to PIPELINE with category context.
If deliverables are present, a deliverable row can route to PIPELINE TASK with that deliverable preselected.
NORMATIVE and EVALUATIVE matrix cells route to WORKBENCH.
OPERATIVE matrix cells route to PIPELINE.
Disabled or unsupported matrix variants remain visible as coming soon rather than silently disappearing.
Execution-root scaffolding starts after the user selects a working root.
The user provides a decomposition markdown path and coordination mode before scaffolding.
The app calls POST /api/harness/scaffold to scaffold an execution root.
The scaffold runtime parses package and deliverable tables, creates tool roots, copies decomposition, writes INIT.md, writes coordination metadata, creates folders, and returns validation summaries.
Scaffolding is idempotent for existing directories and files.
Scaffolding failures are fail-fast and include stage, target path, and created paths for recovery.
PREPARATION compatibility is reported before the user proceeds with scaffolding.
Workbench persona sessions begin when the user routes to WORKBENCH with an agent persona.
The chat panel resolves persona aliases to instruction-file names.
The user can send a prompt with optional runtime options and attachments.
The app creates or boots a harness session when needed.
The runtime streams turn events to the UI.
The user may interrupt a running turn.
Session identity is preserved across turns for the same root, persona, and mode.
Runtime errors preserve the draft and attachments for retry.
Interrupt returns a terminal process:exit event and updates UI state.
Operative pipeline intent starts when the user opens PIPELINE.
The user selects one of DECOMP, PREP, TASK, or AUDIT in PIPELINE.
The user selects a category-specific agent or lane in PIPELINE.
For TASK, the user selects scope mode and dynamic scope from the working root.
The user can inspect deliverable status and dependency contract snapshots and apply allowed lifecycle transitions.
Deliverable selections reset when the project root or scan results become stale.
KNOWLEDGE_TYPES mode is shown only when a knowledge decomposition marker is detected.
Lifecycle transitions enforce authorized actors and approval SHA requirements for human gate states.
File attachment starts when the user opens the file picker from Chat Panel.
The user selects supported files by absolute path.
The UI previews attachments as non-authoritative client metadata.
The server validates, classifies, and reads attachments.
A turn proceeds if user text exists or at least one valid attachment resolves.
Allowed attachment extensions are png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, pdf, txt, md, and csv.
Symlinks, directories, special files, unsupported extensions, unreadable files, files over 10 MB, and total raw bytes over 18 MB are rejected.
Partial attachment failure is non-fatal when executable content remains.
If all attachments fail and text is empty, the request fails with ATTACHMENT_FAILURE.
API key storage starts when the user opens API key settings.
The user stores an API key through Electron IPC.
Electron encrypts API key material with safeStorage outside the working root.
The server runtime reads the UI key from process global and otherwise uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
API key material is never written to working-root files.
The UI API key takes precedence over environment keys.
API key status can report source as ui, env, or none.
If secure storage is unavailable, the UI reports an error.
Release validation starts when the release operator installs dependencies in frontend.
The release operator runs tests, typecheck, and harness validation.
The release operator runs the desktop distribution build.
The build packages app resources and verifies instruction-root integrity.
The packaging acceptance output includes frontend/dist/Chirality-0.1.0-arm64.dmg for macOS arm64.
The app bundle includes agents and docs.
The app minimum macOS target is 15.0.0 or later.
The build is unsigned or adhoc by design.
P0 priority means required for current release usefulness and safety.
P1 priority means important for current release quality or governed operation.
P2 priority means desirable or future hardening.
FR-001 P0 requires a desktop shell with PORTAL, PIPELINE, and WORKBENCH navigation and active-route indication.
FR-002 P0 requires global working-root selection with type, folder choose, apply, and clear controls.
FR-003 P0 requires working-root validation to fail typed errors for non-absolute, missing, inaccessible, non-directory, or instruction-root-contained paths.
FR-004 P0 requires a selected-root file tree that skips excluded build and dependency directories, bounds depth, and marks inaccessible directory truncation.
FR-005 P1 requires resizable and collapsible File Tree, Toolkit, and Chat panes with drag, keyboard resize, Home collapse, End expand, and local persistence.
FR-006 P1 requires a calm, professional, dense-but-readable UI with no regression against the UI polish acceptance plan or harness behavior.
FR-007 P0 requires PORTAL to render the 3x4 agent matrix using NORMATIVE, OPERATIVE, EVALUATIVE rows and GUIDING, APPLYING, JUDGING, REVIEWING columns.
FR-008 P0 requires matrix routing to follow docs/SPEC with NORMATIVE and EVALUATIVE cells opening WORKBENCH and OPERATIVE cells opening PIPELINE categories.
FR-009 P0 requires WORKBENCH to present selected agent, row, and column from query params with sensible defaults.
FR-010 P1 requires WORKBENCH to consume deliverable contract APIs for read-only checks and permitted lifecycle transitions, disabling unsupported-agent controls.
FR-011 P0 requires PIPELINE to expose DECOMP, PREP, TASK, and AUDIT category controls with documented options and disabled coming-soon unsupported options.
FR-012 P0 requires PIPELINE TASK to use split selectors for task agent and scope, with scope mode DELIVERABLES or KNOWLEDGE_TYPES.
FR-013 P1 requires dynamic scope scan to reset invalid selections after root changes, removed deliverables, disabled knowledge markers, or stale knowledge targets.
FR-014 P0 requires create, list, resume, save, and delete harness sessions stored as JSON under .chirality/sessions or CHIRALITY_SESSION_ROOT and filtered by normalized project root.
FR-015 P0 requires session creation to bind projectRoot, persona, and mode while rejecting invalid project roots and defaulting missing persona or mode.
FR-016 P0 requires session boot to accept runtime options and record boot metadata.
FR-017 P0 requires turn execution to stream Server-Sent Events including session, chat, tool, error, and process-exit events.
FR-018 P0 requires only one active turn per session, with concurrent attempts returning TURN_IN_PROGRESS.
FR-019 P0 requires users to interrupt active turns through POST /api/harness/interrupt, aborting the provider request and yielding interrupted process:exit.
FR-020 P1 requires typed actionable runtime errors in the UI and draft preservation for retry.
FR-021 P0 requires deterministic runtime option fallback chains for model, tools, and max turns.
FR-022 P0 requires unknown runtime option keys to be ignored with warnings without breaking turns or silently mutating behavior.
FR-023 P0 requires persona names to resolve to agents/AGENT_*.md and missing personas to return PERSONA_NOT_FOUND.
FR-024 P0 requires persona aliases to map UI labels to canonical agents including HELP, ORCHESTRATE, AGGREGATE, RECONCILING, and AGENTS.
FR-025 P0 requires production provider mode to support the Anthropic SDK while preserving default or stub testability.
FR-026 P1 requires provider requests to include selected agent instruction and root context plus working-root constraints.
FR-027 P0 requires Anthropic API key resolution to prefer UI safeStorage key, then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
FR-028 P0 requires key material to remain non-project-truth convenience state and avoid working root, docs, logs, and git-tracked execution files.
FR-029 P0 requires the Anthropic base URL allowlist to accept only https://api.anthropic.com with no credentials and empty or 443 port.
FR-030 P0 requires Electron renderer outbound traffic to be blocked except loopback and Anthropic API, logging policy metadata for canceled requests.
FR-031 P1 requires provider errors to be classified as auth, rate limit, timeout, API, network, invalid base URL, or policy violation with key redaction.
FR-032 P0 requires UI file attachments from the selected working root with navigation, multi-select, preview chips, remove, and clear.
FR-033 P0 requires the server to revalidate client attachment metadata for path, extension, file type, readability, symlink status, and size.
FR-034 P0 requires attachment resolver enforcement of supported extensions, regular files, per-file 10 MB, and total 18 MB raw-byte rules.
FR-035 P0 requires the Anthropic provider to map images, PDFs, and text-like files to supported content blocks.
FR-036 P1 requires resilient attachment failure handling, including warnings for partial failures, rejection for total failure without text, and UI preservation.
FR-037 P1 requires the Toolkit panel to expose per-turn model, tools, max turns, mode, persona, and governance metadata options supported by runtime.
FR-038 P1 requires Toolkit settings to persist locally while remaining non-authoritative and unable to override governance enforcement or project truth.
FR-039 P1 requires chat drafts and attachment selections to persist locally per root, persona, and mode, with malformed records dropped and storage failures warned.
FR-040 P0 requires execution roots to follow docs/SPEC layout with INIT.md, package folders, and tool roots.
FR-041 P0 requires flat package folders named PKG-XX_Label or PKG-XXX_Label with required subfolders and no nested packages.
FR-042 P0 requires deliverable folders named DEL-XX-YY_Label or DEL-XXX-YY_Label, with scanning based on _STATUS.md and valid DEL prefix.
FR-043 P0 requires canonical deliverable metadata files including _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _REFERENCES.md, _SEMANTIC.md, and MEMORY.md expectations.
FR-044 P1 requires document kit files to be first-class knowledge buckets, detecting Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, and Procedure.
FR-045 P0 requires _STATUS.md to be the canonical lifecycle state file, with parser support for Current State, Last Updated, and history.
FR-046 P0 requires lifecycle transitions to be forward-only and actor-authorized, failing unauthorized actors and backward transitions.
FR-047 P0 requires human gate transitions to CHECKING or ISSUED to include 7-to-64-character hex SHA-like approval evidence.
FR-048 P0 requires Dependencies.csv v3.1 parsing and validation of required headers, enum values, identity rules, and warnings through contract APIs.
FR-049 P0 requires active extracted dependency rows to preserve provenance with EvidenceFile and SourceRef or explicit location TBD.
FR-050 P1 requires dependency writes to preserve lifecycle behavior, schema version, host deliverable consistency, and warnings for legacy or invalid data.
FR-051 P0 requires packaged instruction root resources to include agents, docs, AGENTS.md, README.md, WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT.md, and PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md.
FR-052 P0 requires agent instruction files to declare type, class, surface, write-scope, blocking, and output metadata auditable against governance docs.
FR-053 P0 requires Type 2 subagent injection to fail closed unless subagents are enabled and all approval, sealing, allowlist, and candidate conditions hold.
FR-054 P1 requires deterministic tools to remain indexed in tools/REGISTRY.md by category with executable validation scripts.
FR-055 P1 requires snapshot-producing workflows to write immutable timestamped snapshot folders and movable _LATEST.md pointers.
FR-056 P1 requires CHANGE and publication workflows to require explicit approval tokens and SHA checks, with CHANGE rechecking HEAD before approved actions.
FR-057 P0 requires unit and API tests to cover runtime, workspace, lifecycle, dependency, scaffold, attachment, key storage, network policy, and packaging behavior.
FR-058 P0 requires npm run typecheck to pass for Next.js and Electron code.
FR-059 P0 requires repeatable harness premerge validation that creates the Section 8 latest summary JSON with required SDK test IDs.
FR-060 P0 requires npm run desktop:dist to build, package the DMG, and run instruction-root integrity verification.
FR-061 P1 requires CI to validate server readiness and upload a stable harness summary artifact.
POST /api/harness/session/create creates a session bound to projectRoot, persona, and mode.
POST /api/harness/session/boot boots a session and persists boot metadata.
GET /api/harness/session/list lists sessions for a normalized project root.
GET and DELETE /api/harness/session/[id] retrieve or delete a session.
POST /api/harness/turn executes a turn and streams UI events over SSE.
POST /api/harness/interrupt interrupts the active turn for a session.
POST /api/harness/scaffold scaffolds an execution root from decomposition markdown.
POST /api/working-root/validate validates and normalizes a working root.
GET /api/working-root/tree returns a bounded file tree for the selected root.
GET /api/working-root/scope scans deliverables and knowledge-type directories.
GET /api/project/deliverables returns deliverables plus knowledge decomposition metadata.
GET /api/working-root/deliverable/status reads the _STATUS.md snapshot for a deliverable.
POST /api/working-root/deliverable/status/transition applies an allowed lifecycle transition.
GET and PUT /api/working-root/deliverable/dependencies read or write Dependencies.csv snapshot rows.
The turn stream emits named SSE events with JSON payloads.
The turn stream emits session:init events.
The turn stream emits chat:delta events.
The turn stream emits chat:complete events.
The turn stream emits tool:result events.
The turn stream emits session:complete events.
The turn stream emits turn:error events.
The turn stream emits process:exit events.
The turn stream must terminate with process-level completion or error unless the client disconnects and cancel cleanup runs.
The instruction root requires AGENTS.md, README.md, agents, docs, directive, contract, spec, types, and plan entries.
Instruction root may be overridden by CHIRALITY_INSTRUCTION_ROOT, and packaged builds set it to process.resourcesPath.
The working root must be an absolute existing readable and writable directory.
The working root must not be inside the instruction root.
The working root contains project execution state, packages, deliverables, and tool roots.
The working root is the only location where agents write project truth.
The default session store location is {frontend cwd}/.chirality/sessions/*.json.
The session store can be overridden with CHIRALITY_SESSION_ROOT.
Session records include sessionId, projectRoot, persona, mode, timestamps, claudeSessionId, bootFingerprint, bootedAt, and model.
Electron stores API keys at app.getPath(userData)/credentials/api-key.enc.
API keys are encrypted with Electron safeStorage.
The process-global API key value is used by server runtime in packaged same-process builds.
API keys are not project truth.
API keys are not logged.
Execution root entries include INIT.md, package folders, _Aggregation, _Change, _Coordination, _Decomposition, _Estimates, _Reconciliation, _Archive, _Scripts, and _Sources.
Deliverable folders require _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, and _REFERENCES.md metadata.
The minimum PREPARATION fileset also includes _SEMANTIC.md.
The document kit includes Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
Deliverable folders may additionally include Dependencies.csv, MEMORY.md, _SEMANTIC_LENSING.md, and HASH_VERIFICATION_BYPASS.jsonl.
_MEMORY.md is disabled in this project profile.
Dependencies.csv must follow schema version v3.1 with 29 required core columns plus optional extension columns.
Dependency register rows are not deleted when retired.
Dependency register rows track extraction and closure state through FirstSeen, LastSeen, Status, and SatisfactionStatus.
ANCHOR dependency rows connect deliverables to definition and traceability nodes.
EXECUTION dependency rows capture information flow, prerequisites, handoffs, and constraints.

NFR-002 P0 requires API keys not to be written to project files or logs, with provider-error key redaction and Electron userData storage.
NFR-003 P0 requires non-loopback and non-Anthropic renderer requests to be canceled.
NFR-004 P0 requires symlink attachments to be rejected before provider execution.
NFR-005 P0 requires runtime rejection of working roots that conflict with the instruction root.
NFR-006 P0 requires harness turns to be cancellable, aborting provider requests and releasing the session lock.
NFR-007 P0 requires harness and workspace errors to expose type, status, message, and details where applicable.
NFR-008 P1 requires scaffolding to be idempotent and recoverable, preserving existing paths and reporting failure stage and created path inventory.
NFR-009 P1 requires file scans to enforce tree and scope scan depth and count limits.
NFR-010 P1 requires responsive working-root scans by capping scope directories at 2500 and depth at 8, and tree entries at 60 per directory and depth 6.

NFR-012 P1 requires per-file and per-turn raw-byte attachment budgets before provider calls.

NFR-018 P1 requires validation artifacts to be stable, reviewable, deterministic in path, and uploaded in CI.
Required local checks from frontend are npm run test, npm run typecheck, npm run harness:validate:premerge, and npm run instruction-root:integrity.
The packaging check is npm run desktop:dist.
Expected packaging outputs include the arm64 DMG, the mac-arm64 Chirality.app bundle, and the latest instruction-root-integrity summary JSON.
Section 8 harness validation verifies server reachability, session CRUD, smoke stream ordering, session persistence, permissions behavior, interrupt behavior, and SDK-native stream handling.

The CI workflow checks out the repository, sets up Node.js 20, installs dependencies, validates script presence, starts the Next server, polls readiness, runs harness premerge validation, verifies the summary, and uploads it.
Manual DMG release verification checks arm64 binary, minimum macOS 15.0.0, adhoc signature without developer TeamIdentifier, bundled agents and docs, and working-root selector launch.
Success metric 1 is that a first-time operator can select a working root, inspect the file tree, and start a WORKBENCH chat turn within one app session.
Success metric 2 is that decomposition markdown can scaffold a SPEC-conformant execution root without manual folder creation.
Success metric 3 is that a deliverable can be scanned, inspected, and transitioned according to lifecycle rules with approval SHA enforcement.
Success metric 4 is that harness premerge validation passes in CI and produces a stable summary artifact.
Success metric 5 is that the desktop DMG builds locally and passes instruction-root integrity checks.
Success metric 6 is that no API key or project truth is written outside its approved storage zone.
Success metric 7 is that unsupported PIPELINE variants remain visible as disabled options, preserving operator awareness of roadmap scope.
KG-001 records that provider turns must include selected agent instructions and working-root governance context before production reliance.
KG-002 accepts current governed-human use when several K-* invariants are enforced by instructions and human review rather than runtime write guards.

KG-005 states that the current release scope is macOS arm64 only and Windows requires explicit scope amendment.
KG-006 excludes deliverable locks, project graph generation, unified run records, and staleness tooling from current release commitments except as future roadmap.
KG-007 requires product copy and UI to preserve draft or decision-support posture until human review.
